Standard: Neck injury criteria apply to all phases of the ejection with and without helmet mounted devices (e.g., night vision goggles or helmet mounted cueing systems). Deployable head and neck protection systems show compliance to the injury standard whether or not the head is in contact with the deployable systems. For crewmembers with a nude weight of 245 lbs: a. The upper neck injury risk is limited to 5% at speeds up to and including 600 KEAS. b. The lower neck injury risk is limited to 5% at speeds up to and including 600 KEAS. For crewmembers with a nude weight of 103 lbs: a. Upper neck injury risk is limited to 5% up to and including 450 KEAS. b. Lower neck injury risk is limited to 5% up to and including 450 KEAS. c. For speeds greater than 450 KEAS, the upper and lower neck injury risk limits increase linearly as a function of speed to a maximum of 50% at 600 KEAS. The upper and lower neck injury limits for crewmember nude weights between 103 and 245 lbs are linearly interpolated. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
(1) Lab test: Data is collected from full system-level dynamic ejection sled testing using instrumented manikins. The neck injury standard applies separately to upper and lower neck injury.
